clue.text: Their members were bound to work under strict supervision

definitions.text: Their members were bound to work under strict supervision

parts.words: Their members were bound to work under strict supervision
parts.note: bound reads as obliged by duty, but these convicts were literally chained together while labouring

explanation.surface: A description of a disciplined workforce whose members owe strict duty to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of convicts were shackled together in a line while doing hard labour under guard.

clue.text: Ordered to get round secure barrier

indicators.note: one word is made to go round the other, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered
to secure a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fence off an area with a secure barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like an anagram signal but is the past tense of bid; 'to get round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon of ships or troops sealing off a port acts as a barrier to traffic.

clue.text: Used in cricket matches that may be drawn

definitions.text: Used in cricket matches that may be drawn

parts.words: Used in cricket matches that may be drawn
parts.note: drawn suggests a tied result, but in cricket the wooden posts are pulled up when play ends for the day

explanation.surface: A remark about cricket games that may finish without a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'drawing' these wooden posts marks close of play; a drawn match is also one with no winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The three upright wooden posts of a cricket wicket are removed at close of play.

clue.text: Oxford banker

parts.note: a banker here is something with banks, a river, not someone who works in a bank

explanation.surface: A financier based in the city of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames is given this name as it flows through Oxford; 'banker' as river is a crossword joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the Thames running through Oxford goes by this local name, and a river has banks.

clue.text: Fresh sand, please, for use by the sea

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made new, so these letters are formed anew in another order

explanation.surface: A request for new sand for the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Promenades along a seafront are built for people strolling beside the coast.

clue.text: Cause amazement, seeing a holy man on his mobile

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters of his are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to see a holy man talking on his mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun or greatly surprise someone is to cause them amazement.

clue.text: Romeo's disposition is melancholic

indicators.note: disposition can mean an arrangement, so the letters of the word before are disposed afresh

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's lovesick Romeo has a gloomy temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a sullen, gloomy, low-spirited mood.

clue.text: Prepare to put out with the rising tide

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Getting ready to set sail as the tide comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns TIDE upwards in this down entry. 'Put out' suggests launching a boat, but means publish.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors get a text ready for publication, putting it out as a book or paper.

clue.text: Personal unpleasantness? Lois has it, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so these letters end up out of order

explanation.surface: A sad confession that Lois suffers from some personal problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad breath is an unpleasant personal condition, hinted at coyly with a question mark.

clue.text: Tried to get a seat, but unsuccessfully!

definitions.text: Tried to get a seat, but unsuccessfully!

parts.words: Tried to get a seat, but unsuccessfully!
parts.note: a seat suggests a chair on a bus, but it is a parliamentary seat sought as an election candidate

explanation.surface: Someone tried to sit down but had to remain on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings fit: a candidate who contested an election, and a passenger left upright with nowhere to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran as a candidate for Parliament, and also stayed upright rather than sitting down.

clue.text: Revenues from company involved in various mines

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece goes within the other
various suggests differing forms, so these letters appear in another order

explanation.surface: A firm earning money from its stakes in several mines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the mines to INMES, and 'involved in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings and receipts coming in are both money received regularly.

clue.text: Guard gives a warning

definitions.meaning: a sentry posted to keep watch
a cry telling someone to beware of danger

explanation.definitionFit: A watchman keeps vigil, and shouting to someone to be careful is an alert of danger.

clue.text: They're often engaged in the movement of transport

definitions.text: They're often engaged in the movement of transport

parts.words: They're often engaged in the movement of transport
parts.note: engaged suggests busy people, but toothed wheels engage, meshing together to drive a vehicle

explanation.surface: Workers who are frequently busy moving goods around.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothed wheels in a vehicle mesh together, or engage, to transmit drive.

clue.text: Guards ordered to go in the Spanish spearhead

parts.note: someone ordered to go is sent
EL is the Spanish word for the
the head, or first letter, of spear is S

explanation.surface: Soldiers are ordered to lead the attack against the Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spearhead' looks like a vanguard but gives the head of 'spear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries posted to watch over a place are its guards.

clue.text: Sea air won't change a place of poor housing

parts.note: a shanty is a song sung by sailors, an air of the sea

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The sea breeze stays the same as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea air' looks like a breeze but is a sailor's song; 'change' rearranges WONT to TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum settlement of makeshift huts is a district of very poor housing.

clue.text: Not the main way to transform desert site

indicators.note: to transform is to change the shape of, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Turning a barren desert spot into something new is unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor road off a main road is a way that is not the principal route.

clue.text: Primary requisites for a sewer

parts.note: sewer suggests a drain, but it is one who sews and needs basic tools

explanation.surface: What a drainage pipe needs first and foremost.
explanation.walkthrough: A sewer here is one who sews, not a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stitching cloth needs a pointed tool and a length of cotton before anything else.

clue.text: Unsteady dogs?

parts.note: unsteady movers stagger and lurch, and the hunting breed bears a name built on that verb

explanation.surface: Dogs that cannot walk straight.
explanation.walkthrough: A lurcher is a cross-bred hunting dog popular in Britain; to lurch is to stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: These crossbred hunting hounds share a name with people who stagger and sway.

clue.text: Resort to a lever to provide lift

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so these letters are put into new order

explanation.surface: Using a lever to raise something heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like 'turn to', but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for the cage carrying people between floors is the British lift.

clue.text: Parts of a lady's wardrobe?

parts.note: parts suggests sections of a cupboard, but the clue means individual garments worn in combination

explanation.surface: The compartments inside a woman's clothes cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirts, blouses and tops sold individually to be mixed and matched are women's clothing items.

clue.text: Excuse to knock up an academic

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to rap is to knock
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: An excuse given for waking a university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAP into PAR. 'Knock up' is British for waking someone by knocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse an offence is to forgive or pardon it.

clue.text: Newly written verse takes a new direction

indicators.note: something written anew is set down differently, so these letters come in new order

explanation.surface: A poet's fresh verse marks a change of style.
explanation.definitionFit: To change course or swerve is to turn in another direction.

clue.text: Watched United compete to get on top

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: to vie is to compete
people united in marriage are wed

explanation.surface: Manchester United play to reach the top of the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get on top' places the compete piece first, above the other, in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Watched and viewed are synonyms for looking at something.

clue.text: Heart so affected sounds can be heard within it

definitions.text: sounds can be heard within it

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so these letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: A heart so moved that every sound reaches it.
explanation.definitionFit: The range within which a voice or noise is audible is one's hearing distance.

clue.text: It's not difficult to name a novel midshipman

definitions.meaning: a task without difficulty is simple
Mr Midshipman ... is an 1836 novel by Captain Frederick Marryat

explanation.surface: Christening the young naval hero of a novel is a simple task.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple means without difficulty, and Marryat's young naval hero, title character of a classic adventure novel, bears this surname.

clue.text: New opera in a natural setting

indicators.note: something new comes in fresh form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new opera staged outdoors among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoors, under the sky rather than inside a building, is a natural setting.

clue.text: Warning that a man is about to cry

definitions.text: Warning that a man is about to cry

parts.words: Warning that a man is about to cry
parts.note: cry suggests weeping, but here it is the shouted announcement of a town crier calling for attention

explanation.surface: A sign that someone is close to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: A town crier made public announcements in the street, opening with this call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional call meaning hear ye, used by criers and court officials to command attention.

clue.text: Initially, surgeons can't operate until really clean

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Surgeons must scrub up thoroughly before operating.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub hard with something abrasive is to clean thoroughly.

clue.text: Miserable? Cheer up!

definitions.meaning: read as an order for sorrow to depart

explanation.definitionFit: The word means looking sad, and split into three it orders sorrow to depart.
